summary: Mongolia waives visas under standing bilateral arrangements for about 30 nationalities — among them the US, Germany, Canada, Japan, South Korea (until the end of 2026), Kazakhstan, Brazil and the UAE — and, for tourism trips of up to 30 days in 2026, for 34 more countries, including most of the EU, the UK, Australia and New Zealand; most remaining travelers apply online for the official Mongolian eVisa.

notes: Exporting antiques, fossils and paleontological finds requires a permit. Buy only from licensed dealers and keep receipts.
Narcotics offenses carry severe penalties; hunting and the export of wildlife trophies require permits arranged in advance.

payments.text: Cards are widely accepted in Ulaanbaatar's hotels, supermarkets and restaurants, but the countryside runs almost entirely on cash — withdraw tögrög before leaving the capital.

safety.text: Mongolia is generally safe for travelers. Petty theft and pickpocketing occur in Ulaanbaatar, especially in crowded markets and around bars at night; in the countryside the main risks are remoteness, road conditions and extreme weather.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Mongolia safety and security

bestTimeToVisit.text: June to September brings mild weather and green steppe — July is peak season around the Naadam festival. Winters are among the coldest of any capital, regularly below -30°C.

idp.text: Mongolia is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

driving.text: Mongolia is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Mongolia yet.

tips.text: The visa waivers for EU (except German), UK, Australian and New Zealand passports rest on a temporary exemption the Government granted 34 countries for tourism in 2026, and South Korea's runs to 31 December 2026. Check with a Mongolian embassy shortly before travel.

Your hotel, landlord or private host must register you with the Immigration Agency within 48 hours of arrival, whatever the length of your stay. If you stay privately, check it has been done — overstaying or missed registration brings fines on departure.
The Naadam festival (around July 11–13) is the best and busiest time to visit. Book flights, hotels and countryside tours months ahead.
Outside Ulaanbaatar, ATMs are scarce and cards rarely work. Carry enough tögrög in cash for the whole countryside leg of your trip.
From November to March temperatures routinely fall below -25°C and rural travel becomes hazardous — winter trips need serious cold-weather gear and an experienced driver.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Mongolia?
faq.answer: Many travelers do not. The US, Germany, Canada, Japan, South Korea, Brazil, the UAE and about 25 other countries have standing visa waivers of 14 to 90 days, and for 2026 the Government has also exempted 34 countries — most of the EU, the UK, Australia and New Zealand — for tourism trips of up to 30 days. Most other nationalities can apply online for the Mongolian eVisa at evisa.mn.

faq.question: How long can EU citizens stay in Mongolia visa-free?
faq.answer: Up to 30 days. Citizens of every EU country except Germany are covered by the exemption the Government of Mongolia granted 34 countries for tourism trips in 2026; Germans have a standing bilateral waiver for up to 30 days. Confirm the status of the 2026 exemption with a Mongolian embassy shortly before travel.

faq.question: How does the Mongolian eVisa work?
faq.answer: You apply online at evisa.mn, pay the fee shown at the payment step and if approved, receive it by e-mail within 48 hours. The tourist eVisa allows a stay of up to 30 days and is accepted at Chinggis Khaan International Airport and major border crossings.

faq.question: How long can US citizens stay in Mongolia?
faq.answer: US passport holders can visit Mongolia visa-free for up to 90 days under a bilateral arrangement in force since 2001. Whoever provides your accommodation must register you with the Immigration Agency within 48 hours of arrival.

faq.question: Do I have to register with immigration in Mongolia?
faq.answer: Yes, whatever the length of your stay, but usually not in person: whoever provides your accommodation — a hotel, a landlord or a private host — must register you with the Immigration Agency within 48 hours of arrival, online or through the agency's mobile app. If you stay privately, check that your host has done it; overstays and missed registration are fined on departure.
